questions.question: Q1. What allows a single flat 4D-printed sheet to fold into a complex 3D shape?

answers.b: Combining materials of different stiffness so deformation localises in soft hinges.
answers.c: Using only one very stiff material.

explanations.a: Incorrect - colour does not drive folding.
explanations.b: Correct - stiffness contrast between active and passive materials localises the bending into hinge regions.
explanations.c: Incorrect - a single stiff material cannot program complex folds.
explanations.d: Incorrect - a fully rigid sheet cannot transform.

questions.question: Q2. The flexural rigidity EI of a rectangular cross-section is proportional to which power of the thickness h?

explanations.a: Incorrect - bending stiffness rises faster than linearly with thickness.
explanations.b: Incorrect - the area moment of inertia scales as h cubed, not squared.
explanations.c: Correct - I = b h^3/12, so EI is proportional to h cubed.
explanations.d: Incorrect - thicker beams are much stiffer, not less.

questions.question: Q3. The stiffness contrast ratio SC is defined as:

answers.c: The sum of the two moduli.
answers.d: The thickness ratio of the layers.

explanations.b: Correct - SC = E_passive/E_active; a high value localises bending in the soft layer.
explanations.c: Incorrect - SC is a ratio, not a sum.
explanations.d: Incorrect - SC compares moduli, not thicknesses.

questions.question: Q4. What does the Grubler-Kutzbach criterion compute for a planar mechanism?

answers.b: Its mobility (number of degrees of freedom).

explanations.a: Incorrect - it is a kinematic, not a mass, calculation.
explanations.b: Correct - F = 3(n-1) - 2 j1 - j2 gives the number of independent motions.
explanations.c: Incorrect - it is unrelated to electrical properties.
explanations.d: Incorrect - it is unrelated to thermal properties.

questions.question: Q5. A planar mechanism computed to have mobility F = 0 is:

answers.a: Free to move with one degree of freedom.
answers.b: A rigid, over-constrained structure that cannot move.

explanations.b: Correct - F = 0 is a statically determinate, locked structure.
explanations.c: Incorrect - floppy corresponds to F greater than the target.
explanations.d: Incorrect - F = 0 is wrong if motion is required.

questions.question: Q6. Forward kinematics of a folding strip maps:

answers.a: A target tip position to the required hinge angles.
answers.b: The hinge angles to the resulting end-effector position.

explanations.b: Correct - forward kinematics accumulates the hinge rotations to give the tip position.

questions.question: Q7. The Miura-ori origami pattern is famous for exhibiting:

answers.b: A negative (auxetic) Poisson's ratio - it expands laterally when stretched.
answers.c: No change in shape when folded.

explanations.a: Incorrect - the in-plane behaviour is auxetic.
explanations.b: Correct - the Miura fold is auxetic, with a negative in-plane Poisson's ratio.
explanations.c: Incorrect - folding strongly changes its footprint.
explanations.d: Incorrect - the property is mechanical, not electrical.

questions.question: Q8. An area ratio A_ratio < 1 for a folded Miura sheet means:

answers.a: The folded footprint is larger than the flat sheet.
answers.b: The folded footprint is smaller than the flat sheet (it contracts).

explanations.a: Incorrect - a ratio below 1 means a smaller footprint.
explanations.b: Correct - A_ratio < 1 means the folded sheet occupies less area, enabling compact deployment.
explanations.c: Incorrect - folding is exactly what produces the contraction.
explanations.d: Incorrect - the ratio describes area, not failure.

questions.question: Q9. Which law is used to predict the fatigue life of a repeatedly folded hinge from its stress?

explanations.a: Incorrect - Hooke's Law relates stress and strain elastically, not fatigue life.
explanations.b: Correct - Basquin's Law N = (sigma_f/sigma_max)^(1/b) predicts cycles to failure.
explanations.d: Incorrect - Beer-Lambert is for light absorption.

questions.question: Q10. Why does a thinner flexure hinge generally survive many more actuation cycles?

answers.b: Because a thinner hinge has a lower peak bending strain and stress, and fatigue life rises steeply as stress falls.

explanations.a: Incorrect - mass is not the factor.
explanations.b: Correct - epsilon_max = h/(2R), so smaller h lowers stress, and N ~ sigma^(-1/b) rises dramatically.
explanations.d: Incorrect - thermal conduction does not set fatigue life here.
